body.title: glab mr merge --rebase --auto-merge doesn't rebase
body.description:
### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: 1.101.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Windows 11
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 18.3.0-ee
  (Use the `version` endpoint, like this: gitlab.my-company.com/api/v4/version) 
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

`glab mr merge --rebase --auto-merge` doesn't work as expected. I expected it does rebase on master then "Set to auto-merge" but it just merges already approved task without rebasing.

body.title: Convert credentialhelper and git-credential to api.Client.Credential
body.description:
## Summary

Finish the work !3805 started: make every consumer of `Client.AuthSource()` go through
`Client.Credential`, so the auth-source-to-credential-kind mapping lives in exactly one place.

!3805 added `Credential` and converted the two consumers no other open MR touched
(`cluster graph`, `opentofu init`). Two remain, both blocked at the time on !3798 and !3794:

- `internal/commands/auth/credentialhelper/credentialhelper.go`
- `internal/commands/auth/login/helper.go`

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Each remaining consumer re-derives whether the credential is OAuth2, and one of them gets it
wrong. `login/helper.go` branches on `cfg.Get(host, "is_oauth2")` rather than on what the
client actually resolved, so with `OAUTH_TOKEN` set and nothing stored for the host it emits
`username=personal-access-token` alongside an OAuth token. Measured on the merged
!3798 + !3794 branches:

```
is_oauth2="" job_token="" token="env-oauth-token" user="" -> takes OAuth branch: false
```

Only `internal/api` knows the answer, because only it applies the `GLAB_IS_OAUTH2` /
variable-provenance / stored-flag precedence. Any consumer that asks configuration instead is
answering a different question.

## Scope

1. `credentialhelper`: replace the type switch and `tokenFromHeader` with `Credential`.
   `tokenFromHeader` recovers the kind by matching the header name and stripping `Bearer `,
   which is information `internal/api` had and discarded.
2. `login/helper.go`: switch on the resolved credential rather than on stored `is_oauth2`,
   which fixes the `OAUTH_TOKEN` case above.
3. Once both are converted, `api.OAuth2AccessTokenOnlyAuthSource` may no longer need to be
   exported.

Note that `AuthSource().Header()` cannot serve `git-credential`: `OAuthTokenSource` and the
access-token-only source both emit `Authorization: Bearer`, but only the first has an expiry
and refresh token to report to Git. `Credential` carries both, which is why it is the right
seam.

## Out of scope

`glab cluster graph` still refuses a personal access token supplied through `OAUTH_TOKEN`,
because KAS accepts only the `pat:` authorization scheme and the token is classified as
OAuth2. That is a separate question about the KAS scheme, not about this seam.

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Scope items 1 and 3 landed in !3798. Only `internal/commands/auth/login/helper.go` is left.

1. In `(*options).run` (`internal/commands/auth/login/helper.go:107`), stop using config to pick the branch. Keep `cfg.Get(host, "user")`, since the PAT username is not part of a credential, and drop the `is_oauth2`, `job_token` and `token` reads. Build the client once for every path: `apiClient, err := o.apiClient(host)`, then `cred, err := apiClient.Credential(ctx)`.
2. Map the errors. `errors.Is(err, api.ErrUnauthenticated)` must return `cmdutils.SilentError`, matching today's `default:` arm at line 153, so Git falls through to the next helper on an unconfigured host instead of failing. Any other error keeps a wrapped message naming the host.
3. Replace the `switch {}` at line 122 with `switch cred.Kind`. `api.CredentialOAuth2` keeps the existing body (username `oauth2`, `password_expiry_utc` when `cred.Expiry` is non-zero, `oauth_refresh_token` when non-empty) but no longer needs the kind re-check at line 133. `api.CredentialJobToken` emits `gitlab-ci-token`. `api.CredentialPAT` emits the configured user, falling back to `personalAccessTokenUsername`. Leave the `expectedParams["username"]` mismatch check and the `capability[]=authtype` preamble untouched.
4. Note the behavior change in the MR description: a host with both `token` and `job_token` stored now authenticates as a PAT, matching `internal/api/client.go:454`, where git-credential previously preferred the job token.
5. Extend `Test_helperRun` in `internal/commands/auth/login/helper_test.go`. Every case now needs an API client, not just the `testOAuth2` ones, so in the runner at line 440 default `tt.opts.apiClient` when nil to `func(repoHost string) (*api.Client, error) { return api.NewClientFromConfig(repoHost, tt.opts.config(), false, "test") }`. Add two cases: a host with stored `is_oauth2: "true"` plus `GITLAB_TOKEN` set, which `internal/api/client.go:371` demotes to a PAT and which errors today; and a host with both `token` and `job_token` stored, asserting the PAT wins. The new env case must not clear `GITLAB_TOKEN` the way the table preamble at line 36 does, so give it its own `t.Setenv`.
6. No help text or flags change, so `make gen-docs` is not needed. Run `go test ./internal/commands/auth/login/...` and `go test ./internal/api/...`.

body.title: Let glab artifact-registry login write Maven's and sbt's config where the tool actually reads it
body.description:
Follow-up from !3710 ([thread](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3710#note_3709462370)), agreed with @timofurrer.

`glab artifact-registry login --sbt` writes `~/.sbt/1.0/credentials.sbt`, and `--maven` writes `~/.m2/settings.xml`. Neither location is fixed, and neither tool exposes an environment variable this command can read, so a user whose tool looks elsewhere gets a green check and a build that still authenticates with nothing.

- **sbt**: the global base is `defaultGlobalBase/<binary version>`, overridable with the JVM property `-Dsbt.global.base` from the sbt command line, `SBT_OPTS`, `JAVA_OPTS` or an `.sbtopts` file ([`BuildPaths.scala` at v1.10.7](https://github.com/sbt/sbt/blob/v1.10.7/main/src/main/scala/sbt/BuildPaths.scala)). The `1.0` segment is the binary version, so it is right for sbt 1.x only. On `develop` the default has moved off `~/.sbt` entirely and is env-driven (`SBT_CONFIG_HOME`, then `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/sbt`, then `LOCALAPPDATA/sbt`, else `user.home/.config/sbt`, see [`SysProp.scala`](https://github.com/sbt/sbt/blob/develop/main/src/main/scala/sbt/internal/SysProp.scala)).
- **maven**: `settings.xml` can be pointed elsewhere with `-s`, so the same shape applies.

`--gradle` and `--npm` need nothing here: !3710 honours `GRADLE_USER_HOME` and `npm_config_userconfig`, which are the variables those tools actually read.

## Proposal

One explicit override for the file this command writes, serving both `--maven` and `--sbt`, rather than an sbt-specific knob. It covers sbt 1.x, sbt 2.x and `-Dsbt.global.base` without modelling any of them.

Parsing `SBT_OPTS` was considered and rejected: it covers one of the several places the property can come from and quietly misses the rest, so whether the login worked would depend on how the user happens to launch sbt. That is the same silent failure the writers are built to avoid, only harder to reason about.

## Current state

!3710 documents the assumption instead: `sbtCredentialsPathFor`'s doc comment says it assumes a stock sbt 1.x, and the `--sbt` bullet in the command's help says an sbt that moved its global base does not read that file.

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Add one `--config-file` flag that overrides the file `--maven` and `--sbt` write. `--docker`, `--gradle` and `--npm` are out of scope: the last two already honour `GRADLE_USER_HOME` and `npm_config_userconfig` (`internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/gradle.go:105`, `npm.go:19`).

1. **Add the flag.** In `NewCmd` (`internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/login.go`), add a `configFile string` field to `options` and register `cmd.Flags().StringVar(&opts.configFile, "config-file", "", "Path to the file to write (Maven/sbt only). Defaults to ~/.m2/settings.xml for --maven and ~/.sbt/1.0/credentials.sbt for --sbt.")`. `--config-file` already exists elsewhere in the tree (`internal/commands/changelog/generate/changelog_generate.go:128`), so the spelling is not new.

2. **Reject the values that cannot work.** In `options.validate`, return a `*cmdutils.FlagError` when `--config-file` is set and the path is a directory, or when it is a relative path you cannot resolve. Follow the existing message shape: start with `invalid --config-file: ...`, never with the flag name capitalized (see the comment above `validate`).

3. **Warn when it does not apply.** In `options.run`, mirror the `--registry-alias` precedent at `login.go:311`: if `o.configFile != "" && !o.maven && !o.sbt`, emit `o.io.LogErrorf("%s --config-file is ignored outside --maven/--sbt logins.\n", o.io.Color().WarnIcon())`. Silently writing the default path while the user named another one is the same "green check, no credential" failure this package is built to avoid.

4. **Thread the resolved path into the writers.** Change `loginMaven(alias, token)` to take the target path and `loginSbt(registry, token)` likewise, resolving it in `run` as `o.configFile` when set and `mavenSettingsPathFor(home)` / `sbtCredentialsPathFor(home)` otherwise. `loginSbt` already calls `upsertLines(sbtCredentialsPathFor(home), ...)` (`sbt.go:136`), and `upsertLines` creates the parent directory itself, so only the path source changes. In `loginMaven` (`maven.go:148`) replace the `filepath.Join(home, ".m2")` pair with `filepath.Dir(path)` and `path`.

5. **Tests.** Extend `internal/commands/artifactregistry/login/maven_test.go` and `sbt_test.go` with a case each that passes an explicit path under `t.TempDir()` and asserts nothing is written under the home set by `setHome` (the shape `TestLoginGradle` already uses for `GRADLE_USER_HOME` at `gradle_test.go:283`). Add to `login_test.go`: the ignored-flag warning, and the validation error. Updating the existing `loginMaven`/`loginSbt` call sites for the new parameter is mechanical, about 50 lines across the two test files.

6. **Docs.** Update the `--maven` and `--sbt` bullets in `Long`, including the sentence at `login.go:151` that today says an sbt which moved its global base does not read the file, then run `make gen-docs` and commit `docs/source/artifact-registry/login.md` in the same commit.
